title: Banjo and guitar duets and switching chords between instruments
summary: They talk about a duo on television and Julius explains how banjo and guitar chords differ and confuse his playing.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Geez, have you heard this record that's so popular now with the young people from Exodus? What is that, Dick, the guitar and the banjo duet type of thing?
Oh, those two people? I don't know. Yeah, I've seen them on the late show.
They have been on some of the programs.
Yeah, I saw, I've seen them on that show.
Oh, the young people really go hard well, and they compete with each other.
They great, yeah, they great. I mean, I love that.
Well, I've probably heard it, but I don't know it from that name. No, he didn't.
I don't really know what the name is. It's the name of Exodus. It's the guitar.
It's a name from Exodus, I've heard it.
They fight it out together. Anything that one does, the other does.

It's just like if the guitar would make E flat. The banjo would make E flat. The guitar would make E flat minor. The banjo would make E flat minor, but those chords are different. That's what complicates me sometimes. When I play, if I play tonight with my guitar, and I make an E flat 7 or a 9th or a 10th chord on my guitar, then the next night I play my banjo, I have four strings.
You've got to readjust your whole thing.

And sometimes my mind is on the guitar, and I'm trying to hit a 9th chord. And some of the guys look at me, Julius, I know what's the matter. I say, thank you. Then I begin to reflect, and it begin to come to me, you know. But it's complicated. I mean, you just got to be right in there to know what's going on in the pool around the two instruments.
